layout_map:
1. Slide canvas: a light/off-white 4:3-ish slide frame outlined by a thin red rectangle, inset within the 960×540 capture (frame runs roughly x=56–856, y=36–470), leaving grey backing visible along the top and right edges.
2. Title band: two centered lines of bold dark-red text at the top center of the slide frame — "New Kernel Functions can be derived / From other Kernels".
3. Slide-number badge: small pale-yellow circle with an orange-red "32" pinned to the top-right inside the slide frame.
4. Content stack: four white rectangular cards with blue 1px borders, stacked vertically in the left-center of the slide frame, each containing a bold black heading line and a centered color-coded kernel equation.
5. Card 1 — "Sum of Kernels is a Kernel" with the additive formula in blue/red.
6. Card 2 — "Scalar Product of  Kernel is a kernel" with the green-scaled formula.
7. Card 3 — "Product of Kernels is a Kernel" with the multiplicative formula.
8. Card 4 — "Combination of the above rules is a Kernel" with the combined formula; a mouse pointer rests over this card's heading area.
9. Bottom band: a solid black strip spanning the full capture width across the bottom ~50px, cutting across the slide's lower edge and the red frame.
10. Capture quality: 1.0 scale, 960×540, sharp enough to read headings and formulas; the black bottom band and grey outer margins limit judgments about the slide's true bottom edge and canvas fit.
first_glance_test: Within three seconds a viewer understands this is a lecture slide listing four algebraic operations that preserve the kernel property, with the title naming the topic. The four cards are immediately scannable as a sequence of rules, each with one headline and one equation. The 2–3 apparent actions are: read the headline rule, read the corresponding equation, and compare rules across the four cards — all are directly visible; there is no interactive control to discover. The intended focal point is the red title plus the four rules, and the title does win the eye, although the yellow slide-number badge and the saturated red frame pull secondary attention away from the equations. The equation notation (colored K subscripts, `*` for multiplication) presumes familiarity with the course material, which is appropriate for a lecture but not for the parent-facing app context named in the injected VIEW line.
strengths: Title band — top center — the bold dark-red, two-line headline is large, centered, and unmistakably the primary read; the line break splits the claim cleanly.
Content stack — four bordered cards — the blue-bordered white cards on the light ground are crisp, evenly separated, and give the slide a clear repeating structure.
Card interiors — equation rows — each equation is centered under its heading and color-coded by term (blue base, red second term, green scalar), so term roles are separable at a glance.

defects.description: Content stack — card 2 heading — "Scalar Product of  Kernel is a kernel" contains a doubled word space and drops to lowercase "kernel", while the three sibling headings all end with capitalized "Kernel" — inconsistent sibling capitalization and spacing in parallel headings — normalize capitalization and remove the double space.

Content stack — card left edges — the four card boxes' left borders sit on slightly different x positions (cards 1/3 sit a few pixels right of cards 2/4) rather than one shared spine — ragged vertical rhythm in the primary grid — align all four cards to one left edge and one width.

Slide canvas — bottom edge — a solid black band spanning the full capture width covers the bottom ~50px of the slide, intersecting the red frame line and hiding whatever lies below the fourth card — the presentation is visibly cut off at the viewport bottom — letterbox the slide so the full frame is visible inside the canvas.

Slide canvas — outer margins — the slide frame does not fill the 960×540 capture; grey backing shows above and to the right while the bottom is occupied by the black band, so the slide is off-center within its own canvas — inconsistent edge margins read as an uncropped embed — scale and center the slide to the viewport.

Title band + slide-number badge — accent colors — saturated red (title, frame), yellow (badge), blue (borders), green and red (equation terms) all compete at similar intensity with no stated role system — the chrome accents vibrate rather than support the content — reduce saturation/area of the frame and badge so the title and equations own the accent budget.

Card 3 and card 4 — equations — multiplication is written with a bare asterisk (`K₁(a,b) * K₂(a,b)`), a machine-operator glyph inside otherwise typeset mathematics — typographically inconsistent with the italic math setting — use the standard math multiplication sign or centered dot.

Slide-number badge — top-right — the "32" is rendered small in orange on pale yellow with little contrast between glyph and fill, and it sits closer to the frame corner than to any content — the badge reads as a stray sticker and the numeral is at the legibility floor — increase numeral contrast and inset the badge from the frame.

top_3: The black band truncating the slide's bottom edge (section 4, third entry) — the most damaging flaw because it makes the capture look broken rather than styled.
Card left edges sitting on mismatched x positions (section 4, second entry) — the four-rule grid is the slide's main structure and its ragged spine reads as unrefined.
Inconsistent heading capitalization plus the doubled space in card 2 (section 4, first entry) — the most visible copy defect in an otherwise parallel set.
structural_proposal:
1. Slide canvas — bottom black band — remove the overlaying band and letterbox the slide frame so it is fully visible and centered within the 960×540 viewport.
2. Content stack — card grid — lock all four cards to one shared left edge, width, and internal padding so the rule set reads as a single aligned matrix.
3. Slide-number badge — top-right — keep it but reduce its saturation and inset it from the frame, leaving the red title as the only strong title-area accent.
uncertainties: The black bottom strip may be capture/player letterboxing rather than app chrome; I treated it as a visible crop because it covers the slide's red frame line, but this cannot be confirmed from a static image.
The exact card left-edge drift is only a few pixels at 1.0 scale and is reported at medium confidence.
The grey area outside the red frame may be the intended slide backdrop or an uncropped embed; either reading leaves the current inset presentation unpolished.
Interactivity, hover behavior, and whether the red frame belongs to the slide template or the capture tool cannot be determined statically.

The injected VIEW/CAPTURE line describes an app lecture frame at 960×540; the pixels instead show a standalone academic slide, so app-level dark-theme and app-navigation expectations were not applied.
vocabulary_proposals: inset-slide-in-larger-canvas: a presentation slide rendered smaller than its viewport, exposing backing margins on some sides while other sides are cropped or letterboxed, reads as an unpolished embed — scale and center the slide to the canvas or crop it consistently on all edges.

sibling-heading-capitalization-drift: parallel headings in a repeated card set that differ only in trailing capitalization or contain stray double spaces read as copy-paste errors — normalize heading grammar across the set.
machine-operator-in-typeset-math: a text-mode operator such as `*` embedded in otherwise typeset italic mathematics breaks the math register — use the proper mathematical multiplication glyph.
